question:
A block of mass 1 kg is dropped from the top of a building of height 20 m. What will be the velocity with which the block hits the ground?
(Take the value of g = 10 { m/s}² )
solution:
The correct answer is __**20 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The motion of the block is a case of **free fall** under **gravity**. When an object is **dropped**, its **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s**.
 
• To find the **velocity** of the block as it hits the ground, we use the **third equation of motion**: **v² = u² + 2as**.
 
• In this scenario:
 
 
• **Initial velocity (u)** = **0 m/s** (since it is dropped).
 
• **Distance or Height (s)** = **20 m**.
 
• **Acceleration (a)** = **acceleration due to gravity (g)** = **10 m/s²**.
 
 
 
• Substituting these values into the formula:
 
 
• **v² = 0² + 2 * 10 * 20**
 
• **v² = 400**
 
• **v = 20 m/s**.
